topic: What is the prevalence of RT-PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection among screened healthcare workers?

pico.population: Healthcare workers, health-and-social-care workers, or facility staff with source-reported SARS-CoV-2 testing; results must be identifiable for the staff population.
pico.intervention_or_exposure: SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR testing, including routine, symptom-triggered, outbreak-response, or serial testing.
pico.outcome: RT-PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection among healthcare or facility staff. Retain reports with limited, historical, or mixed PCR testing for full-text source-only assessment; do not treat antibody results as PCR outcomes.

eligible_study_designs: primary cross-sectional, cohort, surveillance, outbreak, serial-testing, or retrospective report with HCW-specific RT-PCR data

targets.population_or_subgroup: Source-defined healthcare-worker or facility-staff cohort tested by RT-PCR; preserve symptoms and testing indication.

timepoint_policy.rule: Preserve each source-defined PCR cohort and testing period. Do not combine PCR with antibody results. For serial testing of the same cohort, preserve the first source-defined assessment for primary synthesis.

targets.effect_selection_rule: Treat one independent source-defined PCR cohort as one effect unit. Retain parallel cohorts from a report only when source evidence establishes independent recruitment; prefer the whole cohort over an overlapping respondent or symptomatic subset. For serial measurements of the same cohort, use the first source-defined assessment; do not pool later repeat tests as independent.
extraction_notes: Capture the exact PCR-positive count, matching tested denominator, staff population, symptoms/testing indication, and source-defined period.
Keep RT-PCR and serology separate. A report with potentially relevant PCR findings but no valid cohort denominator remains source-only.
Do not infer integer counts from rounded percentages or combine nested respondent/subgroup counts with the whole cohort.

candidate_capture_policy.record_scope: Capture potentially eligible primary reports and distinct source-defined HCW PCR cohorts, including symptom-triggered, outbreak, retrospective, and mixed serology/PCR reports; defer final quantitative selection.

source_constraints: preserve separate source-defined cohorts only when recruitment independence is supported
prefer whole cohort over overlapping respondent or symptomatic subset
serial testing of the same cohort is not an independent prevalence sample
do not mix RT-PCR and serology
do not infer counts from rounded percentages

selection_rules: Use the explicit source table if prose and table denominators conflict.
Use one independent source-defined healthcare-worker PCR cohort as the unit of synthesis; a report may contribute more than one cohort only when the source establishes independent recruitment.
Prefer a whole source-defined cohort over an overlapping respondent, symptomatic, or other nested subgroup for the same testing period.
For serial measurements of the same cohort, select the first source-defined assessment. Do not pool later repeat tests as independent observations.
Keep PCR outcomes separate from serology. Exclude source-only reports and records without exact RT-PCR-positive events and a matching tested HCW denominator from pooling.
Use explicitly reported source counts; do not infer events from rounded percentages.

Timepoint eligibility: Preserve each source-defined PCR cohort and testing period. Do not combine PCR with antibody results. For serial testing of the same cohort, preserve the first source-defined assessment for primary synthesis.
